title: Long META — Pre-Earnings July 29 + Iran Oil Relief Separates AI Monetization From Capex-Crush Template
entry: $585–610 (intraday July 27-28). META has been caught in the GOOGL AI-capex-crush selloff even though META's AI monetization profile is structurally different. GOOGL guided $195–205B FY2026 AI capex with FCF turning negative; META's equivalent capex guidance ($60–65B FY2026) is roughly one-third the scale, and META's AI investments are already generating revenue through Advantage+ ad targeting, Llama monetization via API licensing, and Ray-Ban AI eyewear. Enter on any intraday dip toward $585–600 on July 27. If META gaps above $615 at the July 28 open (indicating the market has already re-rated before earnings), wait — initiate only within the $585–610 band. The Iran informal mutual pause (Brent $89.73 from $100+ over the weekend) removes the oil-inflation narrative that has been suppressing consumer sentiment and digital ad budgets.
stop_loss: $565 daily close (~5.1% below $595.19 reference) — at $565, META has broken through the GOOGL-selloff support level, implying (1) META's July 29 earnings confirm capex guidance materially above consensus ($65B+) with FCF impairment similar to GOOGL's negative FCF; (2) FOMC July 28–29 delivers a hawkish surprise that compresses all growth multiples simultaneously; or (3) Iran informal pause collapses (strikes resume) and Brent retraces above $97, re-embedding oil-inflation pressure on digital ad budgets. Exit same session on a close below $565 — do not wait for confirmation.
targets: $635 — META reports July 29 AH with Q2 revenue above $43B (advertising revenue re-accelerating above 22% YoY), FY2026 capex guidance confirmed at $60–65B (below GOOGL-template threshold), and FCF positive with $15B+ Q2 FCF; market applies relief re-rating of 10–12x forward EBITDA; +6.7% from $595.19; cover 50% of position at the July 30 open

$675 — Post-earnings re-rating confirms META is the AI monetization winner among Mag-7 with visible revenue from Advantage+, Llama API licensing ($1.5B+ run rate), and Ray-Ban hardware; sell-side upgrades to $700+ PT; oil normalization (Brent $87–90) improves digital ad spend outlook for Q3; cover 40% of remaining position

$720 — Full re-rating: META closes the gap to its pre-GOOGL-selloff levels as the AI capex narrative bifurcates between infrastructure spenders (GOOGL, MSFT) and AI-revenue generators (META); P/E expands from 22x to 26x forward as FCF proves durable; hold final 10% into Q3 earnings
risk_reward: 1:2.5 to Target 2 from $595.19 reference (risk $30.19; T2 reward $79.81)
catalyst: META reports Q2 FY2026 on July 29 AH at the intersection of two positive structural shifts: (1) the Iran informal mutual pause (announced over the weekend of July 26–27) has driven Brent from $100.40 to $89.73, removing the oil-inflation narrative that has suppressed consumer sentiment and digital advertising budgets for the past three weeks; (2) the GOOGL AI capex template — which sent GOOGL -7% on $195–205B FY2026 capex guidance — is structurally inapplicable to META because META's AI capex ($60–65B FY2026) is primarily deployed in revenue-generating infrastructure (Advantage+ ad targeting, Llama API licensing) rather than speculative AI research infrastructure. META at $595.19 has already been pulled down approximately 8–10% from its pre-GOOGL-selloff level by sector-wide contagion that does not reflect META's differentiated AI monetization story. Q2 earnings is the clearing event.
thesis:
META is the Mag-7 outlier in the AI capex narrative — it is the only company in the group where every dollar of AI capex has a direct revenue line visible in the current quarter's results. GOOGL's $195–205B AI capex is primarily data center infrastructure to support hypothetical future AI workloads; MSFT's Azure AI capex ($170–190B expected FY2027) is visible through Azure revenue but the FCF timeline remains uncertain; META's $60–65B AI capex is deployed across three specific revenue-generating products that are already in the P&L.

Advantage+ advertising: META's AI-driven ad targeting system (Advantage+) has produced documented 22–30% improvement in advertiser ROAS (return on ad spend) across campaigns. Advertisers measure this weekly. At Brent $89.73 (down from $100.40), consumer discretionary spending recovers at the margin, which flows directly into digital advertising budgets within 2–3 weeks as brands respond to improved consumer sentiment. META is the primary beneficiary of a digital ad budget re-acceleration at the scale of the Iran oil relief.

Llama API licensing: META's decision to open-source Llama 3 and charge for API access has generated a meaningful enterprise licensing stream that is growing faster than analyst consensus. The $1.5B+ annual run rate from Llama API licensing is not yet fully embedded in buy-side models. This is pure AI revenue with zero incremental capex — the model is already trained.

Ray-Ban Meta AI eyewear: The hardware-plus-AI-subscription model generates recurring revenue from a $299 device with a $9.99/month AI subscription. At 5M+ units shipped, the subscription run rate is approaching $600M+ annually — a consumer AI revenue stream that has no analogue at GOOGL, MSFT, or AMZN.

The oil normalization from the Iran informal mutual pause is the timing catalyst. Digital advertising budgets correlate with consumer sentiment, and consumer sentiment correlates inversely with gasoline prices. At Brent $100.40, US retail gasoline was approaching $4.75–5.00/gallon — a level that historically compresses discretionary spending and causes brand advertisers to reduce forward ad budgets. At Brent $89.73, retail gasoline falls toward $4.00–4.25/gallon, which is below the psychological threshold for consumer-spending caution. Meta's Q3 guidance on July 29 will reflect the advertiser environment as of July 29 — and that environment improved materially this weekend.

At $595.19, META trades at approximately 22x consensus FY2026 EPS — below its 24–26x historical fair value for a company growing revenue at 18–22% YoY with expanding FCF margins. The GOOGL-contagion selloff created a mispricing that the July 29 earnings event should correct if META's capex guidance ($60–65B) and FCF ($14–16B Q2) confirm the differentiated profile.
bull_case: META Q2 reports revenue of $43.8B (+23% YoY) with FY2026 capex guidance confirmed at $62B and Q2 FCF of $16.2B. Zuckerberg opens the call by explicitly addressing the GOOGL template: 'Our AI investment is generating revenue today, not in 2028.' Stock gaps to $640 at July 30 open. Brent holds $88–91 through August as the Iran pause holds, sustaining digital ad budget tailwinds. META reaches T1 ($635) in the first session post-earnings.
bear_case: META Q2 reports in-line results but FY2026 capex guidance is raised to $68–72B (above the $60–65B market expectation) and management frames it as 'necessary infrastructure for the AI supercycle.' FOMC July 28–29 delivers an explicitly hawkish statement (September hike probability rises to 90%), pulling all growth multiples lower simultaneously. Iran pause collapses by July 30 (strikes resume), Brent retraces to $96+, digital ad budgets re-compress. META falls to $565 stop within 3 sessions.
invalidation: $565 daily close (GOOGL template fully applied to META; capex overrun confirmed); OR META FY2026 capex guidance above $70B (above GOOGL-template-adjusted threshold for META's revenue scale); OR Iran informal pause collapses within 72 hours (Brent above $97 removes the digital-ad budget recovery thesis); OR FOMC July 28–29 delivers a hawkish surprise that compresses September hike probability above 90% with explicit December hike language (terminal rate shock kills growth multiples); OR META Q2 FCF below $12B (FCF impairment at GOOGL scale)
